title: Power Ceilings for Noninferiority Approval with Efficacy and Rare Safety Endpoints
banked_reason: tier=letter below novelty_target=field: the sharp bound is for a newly stipulated product class, not a named published workflow or a demonstrated generic class, and it supplies neither a rate/frontier comparison nor a first bound for an externally established method.

proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal versions repaired literature coverage and added an NP-sharp conditional-IUT power ceiling and proposed certified separation from the unrestricted benchmark. The same N-no-stat-frontier-advance flag recurred because the comparator class was newly stipulated; independent validity review confirmed subfield novelty below the field floor. D0 derivation and Lean formalization never began; the proposal and its numerical certificates remain unproved, and no soundness or structure defect was reported by the proposal reviewer.
tldr: Separate efficacy and total-conditioned rare-safety approval gates face a sharp power ceiling in the stipulated noninferiority experiment. For the full canonical conditional intersection--union class, the ceiling at a legal safe point is attained by the Gaussian upper-tail rule and randomized conditional-binomial lower-tail rules, with outward-certified power at most \(0.01686\). The unrestricted randomized approval frontier has an independently certified lower bound \(0.06349\), yielding a worst-safe power gap of at least \(0.04663\) against the entire class. The unrestricted frontier retains the full unsafe union, separated safe domain and original-record rule space. Uniform two-way Gaussian--Poisson experiment transfer and exact original-table calibration connect this benchmark to attainable finite-trial decisions. Least-favorable support geometry remains an open-ended question. This is a subfield benchmark for prospectively adding a rare-safety mandate to reduced-burden treatment approval.
gap: Classical least-favorable-pair and capacity theory in \cite{HuberStrassen1973Capacities}, generic testing optimization and exact co-primary designs are established. A comparison of one intersection--union test does not quantify the cost of the whole conditional factorization class. The stipulated Gaussian--Poisson approval problem requires a complete-domain value/rule certificate, a sharp conditional-class ceiling, mixed-experiment transfer for unrestricted decisions, and exact original-record attainment. Primary-source restriction comparisons for Ristl and Wellek, Huber--Strassen theorem-level applicability, and the separate 2026 conference-slide comparison remain externally unverifiable.
fill: Theorem 3 gives the sharp pointwise ceiling for the complete canonical conditional intersection--union class and a certified worst-safe power separation of at least \(0.04663\). Theorem 2 supplies the unrestricted frontier and inspectable arbitrary-tolerance value/rule witnesses. Theorems 1 and 4 give uniform two-way experiment transfer and exactly valid original-record attainment. The open question identifies the actual least-favorable saddle.
